    Chick mortality as a result of other causes

    calc_othermortality.Rd

    Chicks can be lost from other causes such as flooding, storms etc. This function calculates the probability of death and then uses rbinom to remove some chicks according to that probability.A fixed seasonal mortality rate is distributed evenly across all model time steps, and a stochastic draw is used to determine whether mortality occurs during the current time step.

    Usage

    calc_othermortality(CoD, alive, seasonlength)

    Arguments

    CoD

    Current cause of death. Typically "none" if the chick is alive.

    alive

    Indicator of whether the chick is currently alive (1) or dead (0).

    seasonlength

    Number of time steps in the breeding season.

    Value

    A character string giving the updated cause of death. Returns the original value of CoD if the chick survives.

    Details

    The function assumes a total background chick mortality rate of 5% across the breeding season. This seasonal probability is converted into an equivalent mortality probability for a single time step:

    $$P(death) = 1 - (1 - 0.05)^{1/seasonlength}$$

    Mortality is then determined using a binomial random draw. If mortality occurs, the cause of death is updated to "other".

    See also

    calc_chickcare(), calc_unattendmortality()

    Examples

    # Living chick exposed to background mortality
calc_othermortality(
  CoD = "none",
  alive = 1,
  seasonlength = 40
)
#> [1] "none"

# Repeat many times to estimate mortality frequency
mortality <- replicate(
  1000,
  calc_othermortality(
    CoD = "none",
    alive = 1,
    seasonlength = 40
  )
)

table(mortality)
#> mortality
#>  none other 
#>   999     1
